mathcounts-potw-2026-08-17-01.prompt: At Summer's annual physical exam on May 31st, her height was determined to be 4 feet and 3 inches. Summer last visited the doctor the previous year on September 28th at which time her height was 3 feet and $11\frac12$ inches. Based on this data, on average, how many inches did Summer grow each day? (February had 28 days.) Express your answer as a common fraction.

mathcounts-potw-2026-08-17-02.prompt: At Summer's last doctor visit on September 28 her height was 3 feet $11\frac12$ inches, and at her annual physical exam on May 31st (the following year, not a leap year) her height was 4 feet 3 inches. Summer wants to ride the Shocker roller coaster before returning to school. Unfortunately, this roller coaster has a minimum height restriction of $4\frac12$ ft. Summer measured herself on August 16th, and she is still not tall enough. If Summer maintained her average rate of growth between those two doctor visits since May 31st, how many inches does Summer need to grow during the rest of her summer break in order to meet the minimum height restriction and ride the Shocker? Express your answer as a mixed number in simplest form.

mathcounts-potw-2026-08-17-03.prompt: At Summer's last doctor visit on September 28 her height was 3 feet $11\frac12$ inches, and at her annual physical exam on May 31st (the following year, not a leap year) her height was 4 feet 3 inches.
